error_analysis.note: Segments with fewer than 20 relevant rows are omitted -- too little data for a reliable rate. A segment's rate is flagged elevated_* when it exceeds the overall rate by at least 0.10 absolute or 50% relative, whichever is larger.
error_analysis.detection_note: Segment columns auto-detected as feature-matrix columns with between 2 and 50 distinct values (the generic post-encoding signature of a categorical column): ['customer_state', 'max_installments', 'primary_seller_state', 'n_items', 'n_distinct_products'].

test_predictions_table.note: Sampled 5000 of 19296 held-out test rows (fixed seed=42) to keep the report size manageable -- the CSV download and dashboard table below reflect only this sample, not the full test set.

calibration_note: This model uses class_weight='balanced' to handle class imbalance, which systematically shifts predict_proba outputs away from true probabilities -- exactly what a calibration curve measures. Treat a decision threshold (e.g. threshold=0.3 in the threshold sweep) as a precision/recall cutoff chosen for a business tradeoff, not a literal percentage chance of the outcome. Measured ECE = 0.3166 exceeded the 0.05 threshold, so a isotonic-calibrated comparison model was fit ('HistGradientBoostingClassifier' + CalibratedClassifierCV, cv=3). Its ECE = 0.0043 vs. the raw model's 0.3166 (lower is better). This comparison is diagnostic only -- the serialized production model is still the raw, uncalibrated estimator.
nested_cv_note: De-biased nested-CV estimate for 'HistGradientBoostingClassifier' across 3 outer folds (hyperparameters re-tuned independently per outer fold): f1_macro=0.5671 ± 0.0034. A large gap against the model-selection CV score above means that score was optimistic. Model-selection score for comparison: f1_macro=0.5738.
